title: Technology Risk Director (Hybrid)
description: At Broadridge, we've built a culture where the highest goal is to empower others to accomplish more. If you’re passionate about developing your career, while helping others along the way, come join the Broadridge team. Broadridge is seeking a Technology Risk Director to join our growing Technology Risk organization. This role will support the identification, assessment, monitoring, and reporting of technology risks across infrastructure, cloud platforms, applications, cybersecurity, data, and emerging technologies. The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical background combined with a risk management mindset and an understanding of modern technology environments. The role requires close collaboration with engineering, infrastructure, cybersecurity, architecture, and business teams to ensure technology risks are effectively identified, assessed, and managed. Responsibilities Technology Risk Management Conduct technology risk assessments across infrastructure, applications, cloud platforms, and technology services. Identify technology risks, control gaps, and potential business impacts. Evaluate inherent and residual risks and support risk treatment planning. Monitor and track technology risk remediation activities through closure. Support Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) and technology risk governance activities. Technology Governance & Risk Oversight Partner with technology teams to ensure risks are appropriately identified, documented, and managed. Review new technology initiatives, architecture changes, and strategic programs from a risk perspective. Provide effective challenge and independent risk perspectives on technology decisions. Support the development and maintenance of technology risk policies, standards, and governance processes. Cloud, Infrastructure & Application Risk Assess risks associated with cloud environments, infrastructure platforms, applications, and technology operations. Review identity and access management, resilience, availability, data protection, and security controls from a risk perspective. Evaluate risks associated with modern architectures including APIs, microservices, containers, and cloud-native platforms. Support technology resilience and recovery risk assessments. Emerging Technology & AI Risk Support governance and risk assessments for Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI solutions. Evaluate risks related to data privacy, model governance, explainability, security, and responsible AI practices. Monitor emerging technology trends and assess associated risk implications. Assist in developing risk management approaches for emerging technologies and innovation initiatives. Automation & Continuous Risk Monitoring Leverage automation and analytics to improve technology risk identification and monitoring. Develop dashboards, reporting, and risk metrics using tools such as Python, SQL, Power BI, or similar technologies. Support continuous monitoring capabilities for key technology risk indicators. Identify opportunities to streamline risk processes through automation and AI-enabled solutions. Risk Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement Prepare risk reports, dashboards, and management presentations. Support development of Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and technology risk metrics. Communicate technology risks clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Partner with global technology, cybersecurity, compliance, and enterprise risk teams. Qualifications 5+ years of experience in Technology Risk, Information Security, Technology Governance, Cyber Risk, Cloud Risk, Infrastructure Engineering, Technology Operations, or related disciplines. Experience working within large-scale enterprise technology environments. Experience assessing risks associated with cloud, infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, or technology transformation initiatives. Technical Knowledge Strong understanding of several of the following areas: Cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) Infrastructure and platform technologies Identity and Access Management (IAM) Cybersecurity principles and controls Networking and distributed systems Application development and SDLC DevOps and CI/CD practices Databases and data management Technology resilience and disaster recovery APIs, containers, and microservices architectures Automation & Analytics Experience with one or more of the following: Python SQL Power BI Power Automate Tableau Data analytics and reporting platforms AI & Emerging Technology Knowledge Understanding of Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI technologies. Knowledge of AI governance, responsible AI principles, and technology risk implications. Awareness of emerging technology trends and associated risk management considerations. Frameworks & Standards Familiarity with technology risk and cybersecurity frameworks such as: NIST Cybersecurity Framework NIST AI Risk Management Framework COBIT CIS Controls FFIEC Technology Risk Guidance ISO 27001 Certifications (Preferred) One or more

title: Enterprise Risk Management, Vice President
description: Vice President, ERM Controls & Assurance Position Summary The Vice President, ERM Controls & Assurance, will support the Head of ERM Controls & Assurance in providing governance, oversight, and reporting for ERM-owned risks, issues, and controls. The role is responsible for driving effective issue management, control governance, assurance activities, and risk assessment processes across Enterprise Risk Management. The Vice President will work closely with ERM leadership, Corporate Audit, Operational Risk, Compliance, and other stakeholders to strengthen the control environment, drive issue remediation and assessment activities, and deliver reporting and analysis for senior management and governance committees. Key Responsibilities Issues & Controls Provide governance and oversight of ERM-owned issues, including regulatory findings, audit issues, and self-identified issues, and coordinate related reporting, escalation, and governance activities, including preparation of materials for the ERM and Corporate Compliance Business Risk Committee. Partner with ERM risk teams to assess control design and effectiveness, monitor trends across issues and controls, and identify opportunities for control enhancement and risk mitigation. Oversee maintenance and governance of the ERM control inventory within Archer. Assessments Support execution of the semi-annual ERM Risk Scorecard process. Coordinate quarterly control environment assessments and reporting. Support and challenge Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) in partnership with Operational Risk. Develop analysis, reporting, and presentations regarding control effectiveness, issue trends, remediation progress, and overall control environment health for senior management and governance committees. Assurance Coordinate ERM-related audit engagement activities, including requests, responses, management action tracking, and reporting. Assist in the development and review of remediation plans, closure packages, and sustainability assessments, providing effective challenge to promote sustainable outcomes. Monitor audit and regulatory commitments and report on remediation progress, key milestones, and emerging risks. Leadership & Stakeholder Management Facilitate cross-functional working groups and represent the Controls & Assurance function in governance forums and committee discussions. Build effective working relationships across ERM to facilitate issue resolution, assessments, and control enhancement activities. Qualifications Required 8+ years of experience in Risk Management, Controls, Internal Audit, Operational Risk, Regulatory Remediation, or Assurance functions. Strong understanding of control frameworks, issue management, control assessments, and assurance practices. Experience supporting regulatory and audit-related remediation programs and issue management activities. Demonstrated ability to prepare executive-level reporting and committee materials. Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills. Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive cross-functional initiatives. Preferred Experience with Archer, RCSA processes, issue management, and control inventories. Experience supporting interactions with regulators and Internal Audit. Knowledge of risk reporting, control effectiveness assessments, and financial services regulatory expectations. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ. title: Security GRC Lead

Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. The internal trust narrative: customer trust pages, security one-pagers, executive-ready disclosure templates when something goes sideways WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 7+ years in security GRC, compliance engineering, or audit, with at least 2 years owning a SOC 2 Type 2 program end-to-end at a company under audit by enterprise customers - You've shipped at least one ISO 27001 certification from kickoff to issued certificate, including Stage 1 and Stage 2 with a real registrar - Fluent in Vanta (or Drata, Secureframe, Sprinto) at the integration and admin level, not just the reviewer UI - you've configured connectors, written custom tests, debugged broken evidence - You've sat on the company side of at least one enterprise customer audit conducted by a Big 4 firm (KPMG, EY, Deloitte, PwC) on behalf of a frontier customer - You translate cloud-security language to auditor language and back without losing precision - you can read a Wiz finding, a Panther rule, an IAM policy, and say what control it maps to - You write controls as code or query evidence with SQL when the platform falls short - Python, SQL, or shell, whatever it takes - You know the difference between "we don't have a control for that" and "we have a compensating control" and you don't fabricate the second one - Direct experience with the customer-trust surface: SIG, CAIQ, custom enterprise questionnaires, on-site auditor sessions, disclosure letters under legal review BONUS POINTS - description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role Are you a curious builder who thrives in a fast-moving, data-driven execution role, curious about how AI can turn quality data into real, operational trust? Veeam's business runs on data flowing from four source systems, v-Power for Sales, Marketo for Marketing, NetSuite for Finance, and Workday for HR, through a governed Databricks Lakehouse to certified outputs consumed by Tableau dashboards and AI agents. The Senior Director, AI-Ready Data Governance has authored the strategy for how this gets governed: a federated, pragmatic model, central standards, distributed ownership, sequenced by outcome so scope is committed on evidence rather than ambition. Continuous, agent-driven scoring keeps watching a certified object's quality on an ongoing basis, well past the moment of sign-off. This is a builder and execution role for a deep subject matter expert, with full autonomy to move fast and deliver results. You will lead highly complex, high-visibility initiatives, shape the approach to problems that arrive ambiguous, and influence organizational direction through the standards you set. The strategy, mission, and vision are set. The job is to run Databricks Unity Catalog as the technical backbone and Atlan as the business-facing catalog on top of it, build the certified Bronze-to-Silver-to-Gold pipeline domain by domain, and make certification, lineage, and continuous scoring real enough that governance becomes a standing rhythm rather than a one-off exercise. AI tooling is moving fast enough that the sequence of what gets built when will keep shifting. What does not shift is the outcome bar: certified data, a live trust score behind it, and a named owner for both. This is a job for someone who is curious by default. Someone who would rather have an agent draft the first pass of a lineage map than wait for a meeting about it, who gets energy from ambiguity because the pace of AI tooling means the plan will keep changing, and who treats data quality as something they are personally accountable for at every level, source system to dashboard to agent output, ahead of whatever a report tells them after the fact. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential. Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. title: Director, Cybersecurity

Built to provide a centralized view of risk and compliance, with AI intelligence woven into the platform's core, LogicGate delivers real-time insights and actionable data to help drive current business decisions, with the flexibility to scale alongside evolving business needs. Recognized as a Leader in the GRC Market, LogicGate continues to further solidify its position as a best-in-class platform. Excited about LogicGate but not familiar with GRC?  GRC stands for Governance, Risk, and Compliance GRC professionals help their companies manage uncertainty, act with integrity, and stay on the right side of the law.  The GRC market is rapidly expanding with continuous growth opportunities. The current market size was valued at $50.5 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach $104.5 billion by 2031.   About the Role The Director, Cybersecurity drives the execution of LogicGate’s internal security and compliance program, protecting our SaaS platform and reinforcing enterprise customer trust. Reporting directly to the CISO, you will lead the security organization, operationalize risk management, and scale our SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP compliance frameworks. In a business building GRC software for global enterprises, your security program serves as both a foundational shield and a direct catalyst for enterprise sales. You will develop high-performing security teams, partner cross-functionally across Engineering and Product, and represent our security posture credibly to enterprise buyers. What You’ll Do Program Execution: Operationalize LogicGate’s enterprise security roadmap in partnership with the CISO, translating strategic objectives into daily InfoSec and IT security operations that safeguard customer data and platform integrity. People Leadership: Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing security organization—serving as the Deputy CISO—fostering a culture of continuous learning, accountability, and strong team engagement. title: Lead product manager
description: 🚀 About WRITER WRITER is where the world's leading enterprises orchestrate AI-powered work. Our vision is to expand human capacity through superintelligence. And we're proving it's possible – through powerful, trustworthy AI that unites IT and business teams together to unlock enterprise-wide transformation. Founded in 2020 with office hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Seattle, Austin, Chicago, and London, our team thinks big and moves fast, and we're looking for smart, hardworking builders and scalers to join us on our journey to create a better future of work with AI. 📐 About this role This is a chance to help shape the next chapter of WRITER's product at a moment when generative AI is redefining how work gets done. As senior staff product manager, you'll report directly to Wil Pong, VP of Product, and operate as a force-multiplier across the product organization — setting direction where it's unclear, aligning stakeholders, and making sure our most critical initiatives ship with excellence. You'll own ambiguous, high-impact problem spaces that span multiple product areas and teams, and you'll be equal parts strategist and operator. One moment you're shaping a multi-quarter roadmap; the next you're rolling up your sleeves to unblock execution. We're looking for someone who thrives at the intersection of customer empathy, technical depth, and business judgment — and who is energized by turning complex, evolving AI capabilities into products customers love. 🦸🏻‍♀️ Your responsibilities - Drive high-impact product initiatives end-to-end, from discovery and problem definition through launch, adoption, and iteration across areas that span multiple squads and surfaces - Shape product strategy and roadmap in partnership with the VP of Product and product leadership, translating company-level goals into clear, sequenced, ambitious bets - Spend time with enterprise buyers, end users, and prospects to uncover unmet needs, validate problem-solution fit, and champion the customer voice in every decision - Partner closely with engineering and design to define requirements, navigate technical tradeoffs, and build the right things in the right order, bringing real fluency to conversations about LLMs, agents, platform architecture, and data - Align cross-functional stakeholders across go-to-market, sales, marketing, customer success, and executive leadership, communicating strategy and tradeoffs with crisp, audience-appropriate narrative - Define and own success metrics for your areas, using data and qualitative signal to evaluate impact, course-correct, and tell the story of outcomes to leadership - Raise the bar on product craft across the org by mentoring and coaching other PMs, modeling best practices, and strengthening a culture built on rigor, customer obsession, and velocity ⭐️ Is this you? - 8+ years of product management experience with a track record of owning and shipping complex, high-impact products, ideally in SaaS, platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML-driven environments - Senior- or staff-level experience operating autonomously across ambiguous, multi-team problem spaces and influencing outcomes well beyond your immediate team - Genuine customer obsession — you instinctively go to the customer, synthesize signal from noise, and design from a deep understanding of real workflows and pain points - Technical credibility to engage meaningfully with engineers and researchers on system design, LLM capabilities, data, and architecture, knowing when to go deep and when to defer to the experts - A blend of strong strategic thinking and relentless execution — you can set a compelling vision one moment and sweat the details of a release plan the next - Exceptional communication that you tailor for any audience, from a frontline engineer to the executive team, driving alignment without relying on org chart authority - A mentor's instinct and a builder's drive, with the data-informed, outcome-driven mindset to define success up front and move with the speed this environment demands Nice to haves - Experience building products powered by LLMs, generative AI, or large-scale AI/ML systems - Background in enterprise software, developer platforms, or developer-facing products - Familiarity with AI governance, guardrails, and the operational considerations of deploying AI in regulated or high-stakes environments 🍩 Benefits & perks (US Full-time employees) - Generous PTO, plus company holidays - Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family - Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks) - F
